decisions.reason: The recently launched handle family has incurred sunk tooling and certification costs, and weak early sales can still be attributed to temporary market introduction.
Like the other handle family, the mitred family represents invested design and manufacturing resources, and one year is too soon to judge its full specification potential.
The multifunctional handle has less public commitment than the collections, but its development investment and the possibility of temporary demand weakness make dropping premature.
As a basic lever handle with only a brief market presence, management is inclined to keep it because sunk tooling costs and short-term demand fluctuations can still explain disappointments.
The collection has strong public commitment, its own web page, and an award, indicating both centrality and success, so there is almost no reason to drop it.
The finish has low public visibility and likely lower investment, but it is still new and may be needed across existing product lines, so management probably retains it for now.
